cohort: A cohort of 15,433 infants born at 22 to 28 weeks' gestation in Neonatal Research Network centers from 2006 to 2014.
finding: Delivery characteristics can identify extremely preterm infants with a significantly lower incidence of early-onset sepsis, with low-risk infants having a 0.5% incidence compared to 2.5% in the comparison group (adjusted relative risk = 0.24).
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery, when combined with membrane rupture at delivery and absence of clinical chorioamnionitis, was a key characteristic identifying extremely preterm infants at lower risk for early-onset sepsis.
followup_time: Up to 72 hours for early-onset sepsis definition; prolonged antibiotics assessed for >=5 days.
birth_weight: Measured and adjusted for in regression models.
